CA Bundle Tracker

Which software ships its own Certificate Authority (CA) trust store, and which uses the operating system (OS) store? A reference for how fixes propagate after a CA compromise.

The eMudhra intermediate CA compromise (October 2026)

On 2026-10-17 Mozilla received a report that the private keys of 8 eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised: 6 TLS intermediates trusted by Chrome, Mozilla, Microsoft and Apple, and 2 code-signing intermediates trusted by Microsoft. Mozilla's comment 5 on bug 2083449 states that all 8 private keys were integers less than 256; a later public comment (comment 67) lists the values.

  • 8 compromised private keys: 6 for TLS (Transport Layer Security) server certificates, 2 for code signing.
  • 16 CA certificates carry those keys: each key has one certificate issued by an emSign root and one cross-signed by Sectigo AAA Certificate Services.

Software that bundles its own CA certificates needs its own update: an OS patch does not reach it. Java runtimes, Python environments, Node.js, container images, firmware and Electron apps each carry independent copies that can stay exposed after the OS is fixed.

  • Mozilla bug 2083449 retrieved 2026-11-02
  • Mozilla bug 2083449 comments (REST API) retrieved 2026-11-02
  • Apple support 149555: eMudhra certificate blocking retrieved 2026-11-02

The Sectigo AAA Certificate Services cross-sign path

The compromised intermediates were cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root. Any store that still trusts AAA for TLS accepts the cross-signed copies even after the emSign roots are gone.

Mozilla removed AAA's websites trust bit in April 2025 (bug 1957685, landed in NSS on 2025-04-16). Mozilla-derived bundles taken before that, such as old certifi copies, still trust it. Apple and Microsoft kept trusting AAA and blocked the intermediates by other means (configuration data and the disallowed CTL).

Example: on Amazon Linux 2023 the awscli-2-2.33.15 package ships /usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/awscli/botocore/cacert.pem (dated 2026-02-06) containing AAA Certificate Services. AWS removed AAA from the bundle in AWS CLI 2.38.4.

  • Mozilla bug 1957685: remove websites trust bit from AAA Certificate Services retrieved 2026-11-02
  • AWS CLI v2 changelog retrieved 2026-11-02
  • Apple support 149555: eMudhra certificate blocking retrieved 2026-11-02
  • MSRC: Microsoft response to compromised eMudhra CA keys retrieved 2026-11-02

macOS command-line tools are not covered by Apple's fix

Apple's configuration-data block protects Safari, Mail and apps using Apple's networking frameworks. Tools that read /etc/ssl/cert.pem (Apple names curl, git, python3, ruby, perl and openssl) can still accept the certificates until a future macOS update.

Apple's article gives optional steps to remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services from /etc/ssl/cert.pem. Homebrew's merged cert.pem re-imports macOS keychain roots, so check it as well.

  • Apple support 149555: eMudhra certificate blocking retrieved 2026-11-02

How each vendor pushed the block

2026-10-17: reported to Mozilla at 20:06 UTC; OneCRL entries finished at 22:59 UTC and reached Firefox through Remote Settings the same day. Google shipped a CRLSet blocking the intermediates' public keys at 19:45 UTC.

2026-10-19: Apple began blocking the 12 TLS certificates through configuration data (the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root followed on 2026-10-23). Google Play services delivered the Android block around 22:00 UTC.

2026-10-20: Microsoft updated the Windows disallowed CTL; Mozilla shipped an unscheduled Firefox Release and ESR build for users without Remote Settings.

2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27: Microsoft's out-of-band Windows update and Edge trust-list change removed 7 certificates; Chrome removed emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the Chrome Root Store.

  • Mozilla bug 2083449 retrieved 2026-11-02
  • Google: protecting Chrome and Android users from compromised eMudhra intermediates retrieved 2026-11-02
  • Apple support 149555: eMudhra certificate blocking retrieved 2026-11-02
  • MSRC: Microsoft response to compromised eMudhra CA keys retrieved 2026-11-02

Where fixes arrive last

Android 13 and older without Google Play services: the root store lives on the system partition and changes only with a vendor OS update.

Container images built before the fix keep their bundle until rebuilt; so do Lambda container-image functions and anything with a vendored certifi.

Java applications with a custom javax.net.ssl.trustStore or jssecacerts file gain nothing from a JDK update.

Binaries built with Rust webpki-roots or ESP-IDF's certificate bundle carry the roots compiled in; each one must be rebuilt and redeployed.

  • Android: Conscrypt module retrieved 2026-11-02
  • JSSE reference guide retrieved 2026-11-02
  • webpki-roots README retrieved 2026-11-02

Catalogue

  • Bundled ships its own CA store, independent of the OS
  • OS store uses the operating system trust store (or is the OS store)
  • Fallback OS store first; own roots only when the OS has none
  • Hybrid own store plus roots added to the OS by users or enterprises
  • Configured no default roots; trusts only the CA file the operator configures

Scan your system

The ca-bundle-scanner command-line tool looks for the 16 compromised eMudhra CA certificates (also by public key), the distrusted emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and its issuing CAs, and the Sectigo AAA cross-sign root in trust stores, bundles, binaries and archives on your machine.

cargo install --path scanner
ca-bundle-scanner --profile emudhra

Run ca-bundle-scanner --help for options and exit codes.

Glossary

APEX
Android Pony EXpress, the container format for updatable Android system modules such as Conscrypt.
CA
Certificate Authority: an entity whose certificate vouches for others.
CCADB
Common CA Database, shared by the major root programs.
CRLSet
Chrome's pushed list of blocked certificates and public keys, delivered by the component updater.
CRLite
Firefox's compressed revocation data for all publicly trusted certificates.
CTL
Certificate Trust List; Windows downloads one of trusted roots and one of disallowed certificates.
ESR
Extended Support Release (Firefox).
JDK
Java Development Kit.
NSS
Network Security Services, Mozilla's TLS and certificate library; certdata.txt holds its root list.
OneCRL
Mozilla's pushed list of revoked intermediate certificates, delivered over Remote Settings.
OS
Operating system.
OTA
Over the air: an update delivered to the device without a cable or reinstall.
PEM
Privacy-Enhanced Mail: the base64 text form of a certificate (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----).
SPKI
SubjectPublicKeyInfo: the public key field of a certificate; blocking by SPKI hash covers every certificate with that key.
TLS
Transport Layer Security, the protocol behind HTTPS.
Trust source
Where software gets the roots it trusts: Bundled, OS store, Fallback, Hybrid, or Configured (no default; the operator supplies a CA file).
